name: Pregnenolone
summary: The body's master steroid precursor, sold as a supplement for hormone support; trials exist for psychiatric uses, none for testosterone or looks.
lead: Pregnenolone is a steroid made from cholesterol that serves as the biosynthetic precursor of other steroid hormones, including progesterone, cortisol, DHEA, testosterone and estrogens . It is produced in the adrenal glands, gonads and brain, and is also classed as a neurosteroid . It is sold as an over-the-counter dietary supplement in the United States.
claims: Pregnenolone is the mother hormone, so supplementing raises testosterone
"Pregnenolone steal": caffeine and stress divert it from testosterone to cortisol
Pregnenolone improves mood, anxiety and brain fog
Pregnenolone is needed on TRT to restore a full hormone profile

name: Yohimbine
summary: An alpha-2 blocker stimulant used in cutting stacks for stubborn fat; the fat-loss rationale is mostly untested in men and the side effects are real.
lead: Yohimbine is an indole alkaloid obtained from the bark of the African tree Pausinystalia yohimbe. It acts as a selective antagonist of alpha-2 adrenergic receptors, which raises norepinephrine release and sympathetic activity . It has been used in folk medicine as an aphrodisiac, and prescription yohimbine hydrochloride has been studied for erectile dysfunction .
claims: Yohimbine targets stubborn fat by blocking alpha-2 receptors
Yohimbine works best stacked with carnitine, caffeine and fasted cardio
Yohimbine is a stimulant with strong side effects
Yohimbine improves erections and libido

name: Synephrine
summary: Bitter-orange stimulant sold as the ephedra replacement; small trials show more fat oxidation during exercise, long-term fat loss unproven.
lead: Synephrine is a protoalkaloid of the phenethylamine class found chiefly in the immature fruit of the bitter orange, Citrus aurantium. Its main natural form is p-synephrine . It is a sympathomimetic compound, and extracts are sold in weight-loss and pre-workout supplements, often as a replacement for ephedra .
claims: Synephrine is a safe replacement for ephedra in fat burners
Synephrine increases fat burning

name: Liothyronine (T3)
summary: The active thyroid hormone, a real hypothyroidism drug that cutters misuse for fat loss; the FDA label carries a boxed warning against that.
lead: Liothyronine is the synthetic form of triiodothyronine (T3), the active thyroid hormone, sold in the United States as Cytomel and as generics. It is approved to treat hypothyroidism, to suppress thyroid-stimulating hormone as an adjunct in thyroid cancer care, and in thyroid suppression testing .
claims: T3 helps cut fat by raising metabolism
T3 pills quickly reduce eye-area puffiness
Adding T3 to T4 improves how hypothyroid patients feel

name: Hydroxyapatite (toothpaste)
summary: A fluoride-free remineralising toothpaste built on enamel's own mineral; one 18-month adult trial matched fluoride for caries, whitening claims are thin.
lead: Hydroxyapatite toothpaste contains synthetic hydroxyapatite, a calcium phosphate mineral that is also the main mineral of tooth enamel, in micro- or nano-sized crystals. It is marketed as a fluoride-free alternative for protecting and remineralising enamel . Review authors describe how the particles deposit on and restore demineralised enamel surfaces, and they are being explored as an anti-caries agent without fluoride .

name: Hyaluronic acid filler
summary: The standard injectable filler: reversible gel for lips, cheeks and folds, well studied for volume, rare but serious vascular risks.
lead: Hyaluronic acid (HA) fillers are injectable gels, most often based on cross-linked hyaluronic acid, placed under the skin to restore volume, soften folds and wrinkles, and reshape areas such as the lips, cheeks and nasolabial folds. Hyaluronic acid is a naturally occurring component of skin, and reviews describe HA gels as the most commonly used dermal filler . Well-known product lines include Juvederm and Restylane.
claims: HA filler is a safe, reversible way to change facial proportions
Cheek and midface filler makes the face look more attractive
HA filler stimulates the skin's own collagen

name: Glutathione (IV)
summary: Injected antioxidant sold as a skin-whitening drip; reviews find no proof it works for this and flag anaphylaxis and liver-toxicity risks.
lead: Glutathione is a small antioxidant tripeptide that cells make naturally; intravenous (IV) glutathione is the injected form that is promoted in some countries and cosmetic clinics as a systemic skin-lightening treatment . Proponents of the practice point to laboratory findings that glutathione can inhibit the enzyme tyrosinase and shift melanin production from the darker eumelanin toward the lighter pheomelanin .

name: Eye massage device
summary: Warming or vibrating under-eye massager; studied for dry-eye comfort, but no trial has tested puffiness or dark circles.
lead: An eye massage device is a handheld or wearable gadget that applies gentle vibration, pulsing, pressure or warmth to the skin around the eyes. It is marketed in the beauty and wellness sector for relieving puffiness and dark circles, and in a separate medical and wellness context for eye comfort, with products such as the Foreo Iris named among its examples.

name: Microneedle stamp
summary: Press-in needle stamp for scars, brows and texture; little stamp-specific research, mostly small case series.
lead: A microneedle stamp, also called a derma stamp or microneedle stamping device, is a handheld tool with a flat head of short needles that is pressed vertically into the skin. It is a variant of microneedling, the practice of repeatedly puncturing the skin with fine needles, which is used for scars and skin texture and is discussed on forums for eyebrow and hair areas .
claims: A derma stamp can thicken eyebrows
A stamp can improve acne scars

name: Microneedling pen (electric)
summary: Motorised needle pen for collagen induction; decent small-trial support for scars and texture, but rare reactions and depth/hygiene issues at home.
lead: An electric microneedling pen is a motorised handheld device that drives a cartridge of fine needles rapidly up and down into the skin to create controlled micro-injuries. It is used for acne scars, skin texture, stretch marks, pigmentation disorders and hair thinning, and is a staple of skin and scar discussion in looksmaxxing forums; the Dermapen is the best-known branded example .
claims: Deeper needle depth gives better results, with limits around 1.5 mm
Cheap generic pens work as well as branded ones

name: Straightening hair brush
summary: Heated paddle brush that straightens as you brush; same heat mechanism as a flat iron, with no dedicated research.
lead: A straightening hair brush is a heated paddle-style brush that straightens hair as the user brushes through it, combining the surface of a hairbrush with the heated plates of a flat iron. According to Wikipedia, a ceramic straightening brush was patented in 2013, and Sharon Rabi released the first one under the DAFNI brand in 2015 .

name: Flat iron / hair straightener
summary: Heated clamp plates that straighten or wave hair; the effect is real but temporary and heat damage and burns are the documented downsides.
lead: A flat iron, also called a hair straightener, is a heated styling tool with two plates that clamp and glide along sections of hair to straighten or reshape them. It is used to smooth curly or wavy hair, and also to add bends or loose waves .

name: Hair dryer brush / hot air brush
summary: Brush-dryer hybrid for volume and quick blowouts; claims come from product reviews, with no clinical studies.
lead: A hot air brush, also called a hair dryer brush or blow-dry brush, is a handheld styling tool that combines a brush with heated airflow so that hair can be dried, smoothed and given volume in one pass. Models such as the Revlon One-Step are commonly named examples .

name: Premium multi-styler
summary: A pricey multi-attachment styling tool from Dyson and rivals; its benefits are claimed by makers but untested in published studies.
lead: A premium multi-styler is a high-priced, multi-attachment hair tool that combines drying, curling, smoothing and volumising functions in one device. The category is most closely associated with the Dyson Airwrap, made by the British appliance company Dyson, which also sells hair dryers and other styling tools. Competing products from other manufacturers have followed, and Dyson has taken legal action against at least one rival over patents covering an air-styling device.

name: Wig (lace front)
summary: A hand-tied lace hairline wig that instantly covers hair loss; the effect is removable and no trials have tested it.
lead: A lace front wig is a wig whose front hairline is made from a fine, skin-coloured mesh, usually called hair lace, into which individual hairs are tied by hand so that the hairline appears to grow from the skin. The base is commonly made of French or Swiss lace, and full-lace and partial-lace versions also exist.

name: Hair system / toupee
summary: A custom non-surgical hairpiece for balding men; it covers hair loss while worn, with no trials and documented traction hair loss in some wearers.
lead: A toupee is a hairpiece or partial wig of natural or synthetic hair worn to cover partial baldness or for theatrical purposes; the word comes from the French toupet, meaning a tuft of hair. In modern hair-loss communities the term hair system usually refers to a custom-made, non-surgical hair prosthesis, typically fixed to the scalp with adhesive or tape, that replaces or fills in lost hair.
claims: A hair system is a better option than being bald when treatment is not possible.
Heavy scalp massage can restore a hairline by breaking up skull calcification.

name: Electric shaver (foil/rotary)
summary: A motorised shaver with foil or rotary heads, offered as a lower-irritation alternative to blades; comfort claims come mostly from manufacturer research.
lead: An electric shaver, also called an electric razor, is a handheld grooming device in which a motor drives oscillating or rotating blades behind a protective perforated guard, cutting facial or body hair without direct blade contact with the skin. The two main designs are foil shavers, which use a thin perforated foil over oscillating cutters, and rotary shavers, which use rotating cutting heads.

name: Cartridge razor
summary: The standard multi-blade razor with a disposable head; one 59-man study found it left more redness than a safety razor.
lead: A cartridge razor is a manual razor whose blades, typically two to six or more, are mounted in a disposable plastic cartridge that clips onto a reusable handle. Cartridge and disposable razors have been the predominant type of razor since the 1970s.

name: Straight razor
summary: The traditional folding open razor; popular again as a ritual and a craft, but no studies test its effect on skin or appearance.
lead: A straight razor, also called a cut-throat or open razor, is a single-bladed razor whose blade folds into a protective handle, known as the scales, and which is used for traditional wet shaving. Blades are made of high-carbon or stainless steel and are sharpened by the owner or a professional by honing and stropping.

name: Shaving brush
summary: A bristle brush for lathering soap; reference works credit it with a better lather, no trials exist, and contaminated brushes caused anthrax a century ago.
lead: A shaving brush is a handle with a tuft of bristles used to whip shaving soap or cream into lather with water and apply it to the face before shaving. Bristles are made from badger, boar, horse hair or synthetic fibre, and graded badger hair is the most prized material.

name: Shaving soap / cream
summary: Lubricating soaps, creams, foams and gels for razor shaving; the aim is less friction, but no trials test it.
lead: Shaving soap and shaving cream are lubricating products applied to the face before razor shaving to soften hair through hydration and reduce friction. Forms include hard soap bars or sticks and tubed lather creams that are worked into lather with a brush, brushless creams, aerosol foams and gels.

name: Threading kit
summary: Twisted-thread plucking for brows and face: precise and cheap, temporary, barely studied.
lead: Threading is a hair-removal method, used mainly on eyebrows and facial hair, in which a doubled and twisted cotton or polyester thread is rolled over unwanted hair so that it is pulled out at the follicle . A threading kit is the consumer version of the tool: thread (sometimes with a handle or tensioning aid) that allows the technique to be tried at home rather than at a salon.

name: Sugaring paste
summary: Sugar-lemon paste that pulls hair out like wax; popular as a gentler alternative, with no head-to-head trials.
lead: Sugaring paste is a sticky mixture, traditionally of sugar, water and lemon juice, applied to the skin and removed to pull out hair, and is marketed as an alternative to wax . Sugaring is classed in the medical literature as a form of epilation, grouped with plucking, threading, waxing, lasers and electrolysis .

name: Hair-growth inhibitor lotion
summary: Lotions that slow hair regrowth: one Rx ingredient (eflornithine) has trial data, OTC versions have little.
lead: Hair-growth inhibitor lotions are topical products marketed to slow the regrowth of unwanted body or facial hair, usually after shaving, waxing or plucking. The term covers both a prescription cream and over-the-counter lotions sold as retardants.

name: Whitening toothpaste
summary: Everyday toothpaste with stain-lifting extras: it lightens surface stain in weeks, not the tooth's natural shade.
lead: Whitening toothpaste is toothpaste marketed to make teeth look lighter, using mild abrasives, chemical stain-loosening agents, in some products peroxide, or optical agents such as blue covarine . It is widely sold over the counter as a low-cost alternative to professional bleaching.
claims: Fluoride-free toothpaste is safe and just as good, or fluoride is harmful

name: Mandibular advancement device
summary: A jaw-forward sleep splint for snoring and apnea: a medical device with no appearance evidence.
lead: A mandibular advancement device (MAD) is a custom-made oral appliance worn during sleep that holds the lower jaw slightly forward, used mainly to treat snoring and obstructive sleep apnea . It is a medical device rather than a cosmetic one, and the sources reviewed describe no published research on appearance effects.

name: Orthodontic retainer
summary: The post-braces appliance that keeps teeth where they were moved; proven for retention, untested for jaw growth.
lead: An orthodontic retainer is a custom appliance, either removable (wire-and-acrylic Hawley or clear vacuum-formed plastic) or fixed (a wire bonded behind the front teeth), worn after braces or aligners to hold teeth in their new positions . Its purpose is to limit relapse, the tendency of teeth to drift back, which is attributed to periodontal fibre recoil, soft-tissue pressure, occlusion and continued growth .
claims: Long-term retainer wear "kills" natural forward growth
A retainer can expand the palate or be combined with mewing

name: Palatal expander
summary: Screw-driven upper-jaw widener with solid orthodontic use in kids; adult facial-change claims are largely untested.
lead: A palatal expander is an orthodontic device used to widen the upper jaw so that upper and lower teeth fit together better, most commonly in children and adolescents aged about 8 to 18 . Types include rapid maxillary expansion (RME), slow expansion, mini-implant-assisted expansion (MARPE) and surgically assisted expansion (SARPE) .
claims: A palatal expander can widen the jaw and improve facial structure
Expanders combined with mewing give extra results

name: Orthodontic headgear / facemask
summary: Strap-on orthodontic force appliance for kids' bite and jaw growth; adult facial-change claims lack support.
lead: Orthodontic headgear is an appliance worn partly outside the mouth, anchored by straps to the head or neck, that applies force to the teeth or jaws to correct the bite and guide growth, mainly in children . A reverse-pull headgear or facemask rests on the forehead and chin and uses elastics to pull the upper jaw forward, and is used for underbites .
claims: MARPE plus a facemask can produce forward maxillary growth even in older teens
Growth-hormone or peptide compounds can enhance headgear or facemask results

name: Herbst / twin-block functional appliance
summary: Orthodontic jaw-advancement appliances for growing teens with an overbite; research shows modest lower-jaw gain, mostly in children.
lead: The Herbst appliance and the Twin Block appliance are orthodontic devices known as functional appliances. They are used in growing children and adolescents with a Class II malocclusion, in which the upper front teeth sit forward of the lower ones and the lower jaw is often small or set back relative to the upper jaw. The Herbst is fixed to the teeth and holds the lower jaw forward through telescoping rods, while the Twin Block is a removable pair of acrylic plates that guide the lower jaw forward when the patient bites together.
claims: A Herbst can lengthen a short lower jaw and fix a 'recessed' look
Herbst appliances and rubber bands stunt or recess upper-jaw growth
A mouthguard-type device or home-made appliance can substitute for a Herbst
Functional appliances help the lower third of the face even outside the usual Class II indication
